news.text: 3 July saw a horrific military disaster in the Persian Gulf when the guided-missile cruiser USS Vincennes shot down civilian airliner **Iran Air Flight 655**, killing all 290 passengers and crew aboard. Operating inside Iranian territorial waters amidst skirmishes with Iranian gunboats, American naval operators catastrophically misidentified the climbing Airbus A300 as an attacking Iranian F-14 Tomcat fighter. The tragedy triggered worldwide outrage, plunging US-Iranian diplomatic relations to an icy nadir and accelerating Iranian willingness to accept a UN ceasefire in the Iran-Iraq War.

news.text: 6 July saw the deadliest offshore oil catastrophe in human history unfold when the **Piper Alpha** production platform exploded in the North Sea, 120 miles off the coast of Aberdeen, Scotland. Initiated by a massive gas condensate leak during routine pump maintenance, catastrophic secondary explosions ruptured high-pressure oil lines connected to neighbouring platforms, engulfing the towering steel structure in an unquenchable inferno. One hundred and sixty-seven workers perished, leading to the landmark Cullen Inquiry that permanently transformed offshore oil safety regulations.

news.text: 15 July saw John McTiernan's explosive masterclass *Die Hard* arrive in North American cinemas, redefining the modern action movie landscape. Starring television sitcom actor **Bruce Willis** as barefoot, vest-wearing NYPD detective John McClane opposite British theatre veteran **Alan Rickman** as urbane German terrorist Hans Gruber, the film replaced invincible eighties musclemen with a vulnerable, bloodied everyman trapped inside Los Angeles' Nakatomi Plaza. Critics applauded the razor-sharp pacing and witty dialogue, cementing Willis as a global box-office icon.

news.text: 17 July saw 18-year-old Hawaiian crooner **Glenn Medeiros** take over the top of the UK singles chart with his sweeping teenage ballad *Nothing's Gonna Change My Love for You*. Originally recorded by George Benson, Medeiros had won a local radio talent contest on Kauai with his tender acoustic rendition before the recording blossomed into an international pop phenomenon. The sentimental ballad unseated Bros's *I Owe You Nothing*, providing a gentle soundtrack for summer romances across British high schools.

news.text: 31 July saw Jim Crockett Promotions stage **The Great American Bash 1988** before 13,000 raucous fans at the Baltimore Arena in Maryland, headlined by **Ric Flair** defending his NWA World Heavyweight Championship against Lex Luger. In a fiercely dramatic encounter, Luger appeared on the verge of claiming the gold as he hoisted the champion into his trademark "Torture Rack" submission. Suddenly, ringside officials intervened on behalf of the Maryland State Athletic Commission to award Flair a controversial stoppage victory due to a deep laceration on Luger's forehead, inciting near-riots among frustrated fans.
